StreamingText

Text that isn’t streaming renders in full on the first frame, so history and server renders never animate. StreamingText adds a soft fade on the newest words and a caret while it writes. useSmoothText gives you the pacing alone, to put in front of any renderer, including Markdown.
The caret is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
The full text received so far.
The pacing on its own. Returns the text to show right now and whether it is still catching up.
The text container is a polite live region with aria-busy while it streams, so screen readers announce the reply once it settles instead of every character.
Turn pacing off to render text exactly as received.
Use the hook on its own to smooth the text before any renderer. Streamdown handles unfinished Markdown while it streams; react-markdown works the same way.

When chunks pile up, the pace rises to close the gap in about 0.3 seconds, and once the stream ends the rest is flushed in about 0.12 seconds, so the text never trails far behind the model. Emoji and other multi-part characters are never split mid-reveal, and if the text is replaced rather than appended, as after a regenerate, the reveal restarts from what the two versions share.
When false, the hook returns the text unchanged.
